test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 24 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Given below are three statements and three conclusions. Take the statements to be true even if they are at variance with commonly known facts, and decide whether the conclusion/s follow/s the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All candies are melons.

II. All biscuits are melons.

III. All cakes are biscuits.

**Conclusions:**

I. All cakes are melons.

II. Some candies are biscuits.

III. Some candies are not biscuits.

options.text: Conclusions I and either conclusion II or III follow

solution:
Given statements:

I. All candies are melons.

II. All biscuits are melons.

III. All cakes are biscuits.

The least possible Venn Diagram from the given statements is as follows-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cb7ff74b9666aaba57b504390285f9aff115c0bd734622e59aaa6d8f8935405.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All cakes are melons. **True**. (Since, all cakes are biscuits and all biscuits are melons, therefore, this conclusion is definite and follows. we can clearly infer the relation between cakes and melons.)

II. Some candies are biscuits. False. (This is a possibility but not a definite conclusion, as no direct relationship is given between the two.)

III. Some candies are not biscuits. False. (This is a possibility but not a definite conclusion, as no direct relationship is given between the two.)

**Note:** Conclusions II and III contain the same variable objects and opposite relations. So, conclusion II and III are **complements** of each other, that is either of them can be true.

So, Conclusions I and either conclusion II or III follow. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
